example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, the bank's deposit listing for 1 to 9 October. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

chosen.deposit-listing-1-9-october.csv: the name of the user's own deposit listing file
chosen.crestline-remittance.pdf: the name of the remittance file that Crestline Foods sent
chosen.lakeside-remittance-email.pdf: the name of the remittance email that Lakeside Freight sent

messages.text: Can you apply this week's customer payments to our open invoices?
Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload files?
Which payments: ones already in the books, or a file not yet entered? As of what date do I take the open invoices?
Do you have remittance advices? Where are they?
What difference do you accept on a short or extra payment? I never invent one.
Do I apply the oldest invoice first, or another order?
Is any payment in a different currency from its invoice? If so, which rate do I use, and from what source?
Does any customer withhold tax at source?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. It's the bank's deposit listing for 1 to 9 October, not in the books yet. Open invoices as of today, 9 October. Two remittances attached. $5 for each payment. Oldest first. All US dollars, no withholding.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I apply the **1 to 9 October deposit listing**, **6 payments for $58,997.00**, to **Northbrook Trading**'s open invoices **as of 9 October**. I use **$5 for each payment**, oldest invoice first, and remittances for 2 of the payments. I read the full aging, with no date limit. Shall I start?

messages.label: Read the books in one batch

messages.text: One row of your file is already in the books. Pinnacle Clinics paid **INV-1010** on 8 October, and the books hold that payment. I removed the row, so it gets no second entry.
Here is how I matched the five payments:

messages.after: Two matches need your yes. Harbor sent no remittance, so I matched its name at 0.867 and found one combination of invoices. LAKESIDE FRT INC scores only 0.750 against Lakeside Freight. I matched it by its reference. Do you approve both?

messages.text: Crestline paid **$128** less than INV-0901. Its remittance calls this a 2% prompt-payment discount. But the discount window closed on 31 May, and Crestline paid on 5 October.
messages.after: $128 is more than your $5, and the reason is not valid. So the $128 stays open for collections. I do not write it off or book it as a discount.

messages.text: Lakeside paid **$1,225** less than INV-1032. Credit memo CM-0044 explains $1,200 of it. The remittance says Lakeside sent $3,800, so the last $25 is a bank fee on the wire.
messages.after: INV-1032 is now paid in full. The fee gets its own line in the entry, so you can see it.

messages.text: Two payments wait as **unapplied cash**. They are not revenue.
messages.after: $3,300 fits Acme INV-0990 and Crestline INV-1035 exactly. Please ask both customers for a remittance. No customer record fits J MORALES, so that payment needs research.

messages.text: Here is the proposed entry in your account names, summed by account:
messages.after: The entry balances. The tie-out to the $34,797.00 that I applied shows a difference of $0.00. A person posts this entry. I do not.

messages.text: Your workpaper has five sheets: the summary, the payment-to-invoice map, the exceptions, the posting and the coverage.
messages.after: Do you want the workpaper as an Excel file? And do you want me to save your settings for next time?

messages.text: Done. Here is the Excel file. For Northbrook Trading, I saved the two payer names, the $5 tolerance and the oldest-first order. I never save amounts, remittances or bank details.
